category_title: Students who exhibit initial fear and avoidance but transition to engagement through curiosity and hands-on success
minimal_context: The student is participating in an out-of-school biology workshop session where they are tasked with touching and dissecting a worm.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is the worm for today's activity. Please begin by touching it before we start the dissection.

STUDENT: (Looking at the worm, appearing scared) Have you opened up a worm before? You’re a scientist.

TUTOR: Yes, I have. What do you think you should do next?

STUDENT: I want to grow up to be a scientist.

TUTOR: Okay, then please go ahead and touch the worm.

STUDENT: Ok, I’m going to touch it. One, two, three. (Touches the worm and then screams)

options.A: Implement a time-out procedure, temporarily removing the student from the worm dissection activity and having them sit away from their peers.
options.B: Engage in instructional conversation, validating the student's perception of the instructor as a scientist, and ask follow-up questions like, 'You want to do more of this?'
options.C: Provide direct explanations of the biological anatomy of the worm, detailing the specific structures they will observe during the dissection activity.
options.D: Make explicit reference to workplace expectations, replying that a future boss in a science lab would not care about their fear of the worm.
